file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1901  reply_to=3338867165
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Convert the calendar popover date props**

When `props.calendar` is set to a non-Gregorian calendar and the picker has no current value, `Calendar::init` falls back to `props.today`; this clone is still the default Gregorian date, so the embedded popover opens and emits Gregorian dates even though `ctx.calendar` is Buddhist/Japanese/etc. The selected date is then stored directly by `CalendarSelectDate`, so users get Gregorian segment values unless they type the date manually. Convert `today` (and the forwarded value/min/max dates) into `ctx.calendar` before building `calendar::Props`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GUqtp
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2147  reply_to=3338867169
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebuild date state when the calendar prop changes**

For an uncontrolled picker with an existing value, changing only `Props::calendar` leaves `structure_changed` false, so the visible date segments keep their old calendar fields while `ctx.calendar` starts interpreting future publishes in the new calendar. For example switching a Gregorian `2024-03-15` picker to Buddhist and then editing a time segment can reassemble the stale `2024/03/15` fields as a Buddhist date, committing the wrong ISO day/year. Include calendar changes in this path and convert/rebuild the date value/segments consistently.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GUqtq
file: spec/components/date-time/date-time-picker.md:548  reply_to=3338867171
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove todo placeholders from the spec**

The repo's spec conventions in `AGENTS.md` explicitly forbid TODO/placeholder deferrals in spec files, but this new code example now contains several `todo!()` arms (and a note explaining they stand in for omitted bodies). These placeholders make the spec less authoritative for future implementations and violate the documented review contract; either include the actual specified behavior or replace the snippet with prose that does not use `todo!()` placeholders.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GUqtw
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:947  reply_to=3338867176
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp the initial value during init**

When the picker mounts with `default_value` or a controlled `value` outside `min_value`/`max_value`, `init` stores it unchanged even though later `ValueCommit`/`SyncProps` paths clamp. Because `hidden_input_attrs()` reads `ctx.value.get()`, a form can submit an out-of-range datetime immediately after mount and the segments render that disallowed value until another event happens. Clamp the initial value before creating the `Bindable` or before deriving `date_value`/`time_value`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GUqty
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2213  reply_to=3338867180
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep day ranges in sync with the selected month**

The day segment always advertises and clamps to `1..=31`, so editing an existing February value can display an impossible date that is no longer the committed value: with `2024-02-29`, ArrowUp on the day segment sets the visible segment to `30`, `assemble_date()` fails, and `ctx.value`/the hidden input remain at February 29. Mirror the date-field range refresh here so the day max follows the current month/calendar and the UI cannot diverge from the committed value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GUqt1
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1753  reply_to=3338867184
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Name the popover dialog for assistive tech**

When the calendar popover opens, `Content` exposes `role="dialog"` but no accessible name; unlike `DatePicker::content_attrs`, this leaves screen reader users entering an unnamed dialog even though the trigger only labels the button. Add an `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` (and a localized message if needed) so the dialog is announced with useful context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    pub fn calendar_props(&self) -> calendar::Props {\n        // Project every date the calendar sees into the configured calendar\n        // system so the embedded popover navigates and emits dates in that\n        // calendar (the adapter-injected `today` and the min/max bounds are\n        // otherwise Gregorian).\n        let into_calendar = |date: &CalendarDate| {\n            date.to_calendar(self.ctx.calendar)\n                .unwrap_or_else(|_| date.clone())\n        };\n\n        calendar::Props {\n            id: format!(\"{}-calendar\", self.ctx.ids.id()),\n            value: Some(self.ctx.date_value.clone()),\n            min: self.ctx.min_value.as_ref().map(|dt| into_calendar(dt.date())),\n            max: self.ctx.max_value.as_ref().map(|dt| into_calendar(dt.date())),\n            disabled: self.ctx.disabled,\n            readonly: self.ctx.readonly,\n            is_rtl: self.ctx.is_rtl,\n            visible_months: self.ctx.visible_months,\n            today: into_calendar(&self.ctx.today),\n            ..calendar::Props::default()\n        }\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "            // ── Segment focus / editing ───────────────────────────────────\n            // Focus traversal crosses the date↔time boundary via `all_segments()`,\n            // committing any pending type buffer on the way.\n            Event::FocusSegment(kind) => {\n                let kind = *kind;\n                if !ctx.segment(kind).is_some_and(|seg| seg.is_editable) { return None; }\n                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                    .apply(move |ctx| {\n                        commit_type_buffer(ctx);\n                        ctx.focused_segment = Some(kind);\n                        ctx.type_buffer.clear();\n                    })\n                    .cancel_effect(Effect::TypeBufferCommit))\n            }\n\n            Event::FocusNextSegment => match ctx.focused_segment {\n                Some(current) => {\n                    let next = ctx.next_editable_after(current);\n                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                        .apply(move |ctx| {\n                            commit_type_buffer(ctx);\n                            ctx.type_buffer.clear();\n                            if let Some(next) = next { ctx.focused_segment = Some(next); }\n                        })\n                        .cancel_effect(Effect::TypeBufferCommit))\n                }\n                None => {\n                    let first = ctx.first_editable()?;\n                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                        .apply(move |ctx| { ctx.focused_segment = Some(first); }))\n                }\n            },\n\n            Event::FocusPrevSegment => {\n                let current = ctx.focused_segment?;\n                let previous = ctx.prev_editable_before(current)?;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n                    .apply(move |ctx| {\n                        commit_type_buffer(ctx);\n                        ctx.type_buffer.clear();\n                        ctx.focused_segment = Some(previous);\n                    })\n                    .cancel_effect(Effect::TypeBufferCommit))\n            }\n\n            // Stepping wraps within the (calendar/month-aware) segment range.\n            Event::IncrementSegment { segment } => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let kind = *segment;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.type_buffer.clear();\n                    ctx.increment_segment(kind);\n                    ctx.is_touched = true;\n                    sync_sub_value(ctx, kind);\n                    Machine::maybe_publish(ctx);\n                }).cancel_effect(Effect::TypeBufferCommit))\n            }\n\n            Event::DecrementSegment { segment } => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let kind = *segment;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.type_buffer.clear();\n                    ctx.decrement_segment(kind);\n                    ctx.is_touched = true;\n                    sync_sub_value(ctx, kind);\n                    Machine::maybe_publish(ctx);\n                }).cancel_effect(Effect::TypeBufferCommit))\n            }\n\n            // Type-ahead: numeric digits buffer + auto-advance; the day-period\n            // segment accepts `a`/`p`. See `type_into_segment` below.\n            Event::TypeIntoSegment { segment, ch } => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                type_into_segment(ctx, *segment, *ch)\n            }\n\n            Event::TypeBufferCommit { segment } => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let kind = *segment;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| commit_buffer_for_kind(ctx, kind)))\n            }\n\n            Event::SegmentChange { segment, value } => {\n                if ctx.readonly { return None; }\n                let kind = *segment;\n                let value = *value;\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.set_segment_value(kind, value);\n                    ctx.is_touched = true;\n                    sync_sub_value(ctx, kind);\n                    Machine::maybe_publish(ctx);\n                }))\n            }"

file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:966  reply_to=3341559484
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Project clamped dates back into the active calendar**

When `calendar` is non-Gregorian and a segment edit publishes a datetime outside `min_value`/`max_value`, `clamp_datetime` can return the Gregorian bound supplied in props. Caching `clamped.date()` directly rebuilds the visible segments with Gregorian fields, but later `assemble_date()` interprets those fields using `ctx.calendar`, so a follow-up edit can submit a different ISO date. Reproject the clamped date into `ctx.calendar` before assigning `date_value`, as `init`/`sync_props` already do.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GcP9B
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2194  reply_to=3341559490
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reproject programmatic commits into the configured calendar**

For a non-Gregorian picker, `ValueCommit(Some(...))` normally receives the same canonical Gregorian `CalendarDateTime` shape as `value`/`default_value`, but this path stores that date directly in `date_value`. The UI then shows Gregorian fields (for example `2024` instead of Buddhist `2567`), and the next segment edit reassembles them under `ctx.calendar`, corrupting the selected ISO date. Convert the clamped date with `to_calendar(ctx.calendar)` before rebuilding segments here too.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GcP9H
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:772  reply_to=3341559498
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve era when assembling Japanese dates**

When `calendar == CalendarSystem::Japanese`, an initialized value such as Reiwa 6 displays `year = 6`, but this assembly drops the era and calls `CalendarDate::new` with only year/month/day. Editing any date segment then reinterprets that `6` as a non-era year and commits ISO year 0006 instead of 2024. The DateField path carries an Era segment/current era for this reason; DateTimePicker needs the same era context when rebuilding `CalendarDate`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GcP9M
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2309  reply_to=3341559508
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use calendar-specific month ranges**

This hard-codes the month segment to 1..12 even when the configured calendar has leap months. For example, a Hebrew leap-year value projected into month 13 initializes a segment whose value is 13 while `aria-valuemax` remains 12, and any subsequent month edit is clamped/wrapped away from that valid month. Reuse the calendar backend's `max_months_in_year` logic (as `date_field` does) so calendars with 13-month years remain editable and accurately exposed to AT.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GcP9V
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1865  reply_to=3341559519
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable the hidden input with the picker**

When a disabled `DateTimePicker` has both `name` and a committed value, this hidden input still submits that value with a native form. The forms spec's hidden-input contract carries a `disabled` flag and sets `HtmlAttr::Disabled` for disabled hidden inputs, so this component should mirror `ctx.disabled` here; otherwise disabled date-time fields are excluded visually/interaction-wise but still reach form handlers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "        // The number of days depends on the year/month/calendar, so refresh the\n        // day segment's range whenever either changes (clamping a now-invalid\n        // day, e.g. Feb 30 → 29) so the visible day can never diverge from a\n        // committable date.\n        if matches!(kind, DateSegmentKind::Year | DateSegmentKind::Month) {\n            self.refresh_day_range();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Refreshes the day segment's maximum from the current year/month/calendar\n    /// (via the intl backend), clamping a now-out-of-range day value down.\n    fn refresh_day_range(&mut self) {\n        let year = self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Year);\n        let month = self\n            .segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Month)\n            .and_then(|month| u8::try_from(month).ok());\n\n        let max = match (year, month) {\n            (Some(year), Some(month)) => {\n                i32::from(\n                    self.intl_backend\n                        .days_in_month(&self.calendar, year, month, None),\n                )\n            }\n            _ => 31,\n        };\n\n        if let Some(segment) = self\n            .date_segments\n            .iter_mut()\n            .find(|segment| segment.kind == DateSegmentKind::Day)\n        {\n            segment.max = max;\n            if let Some(value) = segment.value\n                && value > max\n            {\n                segment.value = Some(max);\n                segment.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Day, max);\n            }\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "        // Month/day ranges are calendar- and year-dependent (leap months in\n        // e.g. Hebrew years, varying month lengths), so refresh them whenever\n        // the year or month changes, clamping now-invalid values down so the\n        // visible fields can never diverge from a committable date.\n        if matches!(kind, DateSegmentKind::Year | DateSegmentKind::Month) {\n            self.refresh_date_ranges();\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Refreshes the month and day segment maxima from the current\n    /// year/month/era/calendar (via the intl backend), clamping now-out-of-range\n    /// values down. Month is refreshed first so the day refresh sees a valid\n    /// month.\n    fn refresh_date_ranges(&mut self) {\n        let era = self.current_era();\n        let era_code = era.as_ref().map(|era| era.code.as_str());\n        let year = self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Year);\n\n        // Month range (calendars with 13-month leap years expose month 13).\n        let month_max = year.map_or(12, |year| {\n            i32::from(self.intl_backend.max_months_in_year(&self.calendar, year, era_code))\n        });\n        Self::clamp_segment_max(&mut self.date_segments, DateSegmentKind::Month, month_max);\n\n        // Day range depends on year + (clamped) month.\n        let month = self\n            .segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Month)\n            .and_then(|month| u8::try_from(month).ok());\n        let day_max = match (year, month) {\n            (Some(year), Some(month)) => i32::from(\n                self.intl_backend\n                    .days_in_month(&self.calendar, year, month, era_code),\n            ),\n            _ => 31,\n        };\n        Self::clamp_segment_max(&mut self.date_segments, DateSegmentKind::Day, day_max);\n    }\n\n    /// Sets a date segment's `max`, clamping a now-out-of-range value down.\n    fn clamp_segment_max(segments: &mut [DateSegment], kind: DateSegmentKind, max: i32) {\n        if let Some(segment) = segments.iter_mut().find(|segment| segment.kind == kind) {\n            segment.max = max;\n            if let Some(value) = segment.value\n                && value > max\n            {\n                segment.value = Some(max);\n                segment.text = format_segment_text(kind, max);\n            }\n        }\n    }"
}

=== maybe_publish ===
    fn maybe_publish(ctx: &mut Context) {
        if !ctx.is_complete() {
            return;
        }

        let Some(datetime) = ctx.assemble_datetime() else {
            return;
        };

        let clamped = clamp_datetime(datetime, ctx.min_value.as_ref(), ctx.max_value.as_ref());

        ctx.date_value = Some(clamped.date().clone());
        ctx.time_value = Some(*clamped.time());

        ctx.rebuild_date_segments();
        ctx.rebuild_time_segments();

        ctx.value.set(Some(clamped));
    }
=== apply_value ===
fn apply_value(ctx: &mut Context, value: Option<CalendarDateTime>) {
    let value = value.map(|dt| clamp_datetime(dt, ctx.min_value.as_ref(), ctx.max_value.as_ref()));

    ctx.date_value = value.as_ref().map(|dt| dt.date().clone());
    ctx.time_value = value.as_ref().map(|dt| *dt.time());

    if ctx.value.is_controlled() {
        ctx.value.set(value.clone());
        ctx.value.sync_controlled(Some(value));
    } else {
        ctx.value.set(value);
    }

    ctx.rebuild_date_segments();
    ctx.rebuild_time_segments();
}

  "old_string": "    /// Assemble a `CalendarDate` from current date segment values, using the\n    /// configured `calendar` system (matching `date_field`) so non-Gregorian\n    /// values commit dates in that calendar rather than a Gregorian look-alike.\n    pub fn assemble_date(&self) -> Option<CalendarDate> {\n        let year = self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Year)?;\n        let month = u8::try_from(self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Month)?).ok()?;\n        let day = u8::try_from(self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Day)?).ok()?;\n        CalendarDate::new(self.calendar, &CalendarDateFields {\n            year: Some(year), month: Some(month), day: Some(day), ..CalendarDateFields::default()\n        }).ok()\n    }",
  "new_string": "    /// Assemble a `CalendarDate` from current date segment values, using the\n    /// configured `calendar` system and carrying the current era (matching\n    /// `date_field`) so non-Gregorian values commit dates in that calendar. The\n    /// era is `current_era()` — the value's era, else the calendar's default —\n    /// because `DateTimePicker` has no Era segment (so e.g. Japanese Reiwa 6\n    /// stays Reiwa rather than ISO year 0006).\n    pub fn assemble_date(&self) -> Option<CalendarDate> {\n        let year = self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Year)?;\n        let month = u8::try_from(self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Month)?).ok()?;\n        let day = u8::try_from(self.segment_value(DateSegmentKind::Day)?).ok()?;\n        CalendarDate::new(self.calendar, &CalendarDateFields {\n            era: self.current_era(), year: Some(year), month: Some(month), day: Some(day),\n            ..CalendarDateFields::default()\n        }).ok()\n    }"
}

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Gcxsn
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2476  reply_to=3341745685
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use locale backend when formatting segments**

When `DateTimePicker` is used with a locale/backend that renders native digits or localized day periods (for example Arabic digits or Japanese/Korean AM/PM labels), every segment update funnels through this helper and hardcodes ASCII `yyyy`/`02`/`AM`/`PM`. That makes the composite's visible text and `aria-valuetext` ignore the component's own `intl_backend`, unlike the sibling `TimeField`/`DateField` paths that localize segment digits and day-period labels, so non-English users get incorrectly localized spinbutton values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Gcxsp
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1215  reply_to=3341745688
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear focus when advancing past the last segment**

When the focused segment is the last editable time segment, `ctx.next_editable_after(current)` is `None`; the Tab handler still dispatches `FocusNextSegment`, but this branch leaves the state as `Focused` and keeps `ctx.focused_segment` pointing at the old segment instead of clearing it or requesting trigger focus. In that scenario the component state/`data-ars-focused` remains stale, and adapters that suppress native Tab for managed segment navigation will not move focus to the trigger as specified.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6Gcxsy
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1123  reply_to=3341745698
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear the open flag when sync closes the picker**

When an open picker receives new props that make it disabled, `reconcile_state_after_sync` moves the machine to `Idle`, but this apply block only calls `sync_props` and clears focus; it never resets the public `ctx.open` flag. After that sequence `state`/`api.is_open()` say closed while `Context::open` still says true, so any adapter or consumer reading the context directly can keep rendering or handling the popover as open.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

fn build_date_segments(locale: &Locale, date: Option<&CalendarDate>) -> Vec<DateSegment> {
    let mut year = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Year, 1, 9999, "yyyy");
    let mut month = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Month, 1, 12, "mm");
    let mut day = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Day, 1, 31, "dd");

    if let Some(date) = date {
        year.value = Some(date.year());
        year.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Year, date.year());

        month.value = Some(i32::from(date.month()));
        month.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Month, i32::from(date.month()));

        day.value = Some(i32::from(date.day()));
        day.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Day, i32::from(date.day()));
    }

    let ordered = match date_order(locale) {
        DateOrder::MonthDayYear => [month, day, year],
        DateOrder::DayMonthYear => [day, month, year],
        DateOrder::YearMonthDay => [year, month, day],
    };

    let separator = date_field_separator(locale);

    let mut segments = Vec::with_capacity(5);

    for (index, segment) in ordered.into_iter().enumerate() {
        if index > 0 {
            segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal(&separator));
        }

        segments.push(segment);
    }

    segments
}
fn build_time_segments(
    hour_cycle: HourCycle,
    granularity: TimeGranularity,
    time: Option<&Time>,
) -> Vec<DateSegment> {
    let mut segments = Vec::new();

    let (hour_min, hour_max) = display_hour_range(hour_cycle);

    let mut hour = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Hour, hour_min, hour_max, "hh");

    if let Some(time) = time {
        let display = display_hour(*time, hour_cycle);

        hour.value = Some(display);
        hour.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Hour, display);
    }

    segments.push(hour);

    if granularity >= TimeGranularity::Minute {
        segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal(":"));

        let mut minute = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Minute, 0, 59, "mm");

        if let Some(time) = time {
            let value = i32::from(time.minute());

            minute.value = Some(value);
            minute.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Minute, value);
        }

        segments.push(minute);
    }

    if granularity >= TimeGranularity::Second {
        segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal(":"));

        let mut second = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Second, 0, 59, "ss");

        if let Some(time) = time {
            let value = i32::from(time.second());

            second.value = Some(value);
            second.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::Second, value);
        }

        segments.push(second);
    }

    if has_day_period(hour_cycle) {
        segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal("\u{00A0}"));

        let mut period = DateSegment {
            kind: DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod,
            value: None,
            min: 0,
            max: 1,
            text: String::new(),
            placeholder: "AM".to_string(),
            literal: None,
            is_editable: true,
        };

        if let Some(time) = time {
            let value = i32::from(is_pm(*time));

            period.value = Some(value);
            period.text = format_segment_text(DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod, value);
        }

        segments.push(period);
    }

    segments
}

  "new_string": "fn format_segment_text(\n    backend: &dyn IntlBackend,\n    locale: &Locale,\n    kind: DateSegmentKind,\n    value: i32,\n) -> String {\n    // Route through the locale backend (like `time_field`/`date_field`) so\n    // native digit systems and localized day-period labels are honoured.\n    if kind == DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod {\n        return backend.day_period_label(value == 1, locale);\n    }\n\n    // Year is zero-padded to 4 digits, every other numeric segment to 2.\n    let min_digits = if kind == DateSegmentKind::Year { 4 } else { 2 };\n\n    u32::try_from(value).map_or_else(\n        |_| value.to_string(),\n        |value| {\n            backend.format_segment_digits(\n                value,\n                NonZeroU8::new(min_digits).expect(\"segment width is non-zero\"),\n                locale,\n            )\n        },\n    )\n}"
}

TimeGranularity::Second {\n        segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal(\":\"));\n\n        let mut second = DateSegment::new_numeric(DateSegmentKind::Second, 0, 59, \"ss\");\n\n        if let Some(time) = time {\n            let value = i32::from(time.second());\n\n            second.value = Some(value);\n            second.text = format_segment_text(backend, locale, DateSegmentKind::Second, value);\n        }\n\n        segments.push(second);\n    }\n\n    if has_day_period(hour_cycle) {\n        segments.push(DateSegment::new_literal(\"\\u{00A0}\"));\n\n        let mut period = DateSegment {\n            kind: DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod,\n            value: None,\n            min: 0,\n            max: 1,\n            text: String::new(),\n            placeholder: backend.day_period_label(false, locale),\n            literal: None,\n            is_editable: true,\n        };\n\n        if let Some(time) = time {\n            let value = i32::from(is_pm(*time));\n\n            period.value = Some(value);\n            period.text = format_segment_text(backend, locale, DateSegmentKind::DayPeriod, value);\n        }\n\n        segments.push(period);\n    }\n\n    segments\n}"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale controlled value when becoming uncontrolled**

When a controlled picker is later rendered without `props.value` (for example `Some(Some(dt))` → `None`), this branch drops the controlled override and then immediately reads `ctx.value.get()`, which now exposes the old internal value that was initialized/staged while controlled. That leaves the DateTimePicker visibly filled and keeps submitting the previous hidden-input value even though the parent removed control; the sibling `TimeField` handles this transition by detecting `was_controlled` and clearing/rebuilding instead of preserving the stale controlled value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GdaIU
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_picker/mod.rs:429  reply_to=3341972258
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip bidi marks when choosing DatePicker separators**

For RTL locales such as `ar-EG`, CLDR/Intl short dates include a bidi mark before the slash (for example the separator extracted between the first two numeric runs is `\u{200f}/`). Taking `.chars().next()` therefore chooses the invisible mark as the DatePicker's whole pattern separator, so `format_date` emits dates without the slash and `parse_date` splits user input on the wrong character. The single-character fallback should choose the visible delimiter rather than the first code point of the localized literal.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GdaIe
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2178  reply_to=3341972270
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Localize day-period typing in DateTimePicker**

In locales whose AM/PM labels do not start with ASCII `a`/`p` (for example Japanese or Korean), typing the visible day-period label into the DateTimePicker's `DayPeriod` segment is ignored because this branch only accepts those two English letters. The standalone `TimeField` already routes day-period input through `IntlBackend::day_period_from_char` and its CJK buffering path, so the composite picker regresses the same time-entry flow for localized users.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GdaIm
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1752  reply_to=3341972281
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Announce month segments with localized names**

For populated date segments this uses the rendered segment text as `aria-valuetext`, so month spinbuttons announce values like `03` instead of the localized month name. The sibling `DateField` uses `DateSegment::aria_value_text` for the same segment type, which maps months through the i18n backend; without that here, DateTimePicker users of assistive tech lose the human-readable month announcement whenever a date is selected or edited.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "old_string": "fn default_format_for_locale(locale: &Locale) -> String {\n    // The single-character pattern model takes the first char of the canonical\n    // CLDR-derived inter-field separator (e.g. `ko-KR`'s `. ` degrades to `.`);\n    // [`ars_i18n::date_field_separator`] is the shared source the segmented\n    // `date_field`/`date_time_picker` inputs use in full.\n    let separator = date_field_separator(locale).chars().next().unwrap_or('/');",
  "new_string": "fn default_format_for_locale(locale: &Locale) -> String {\n    // The single-character pattern model takes the first *visible* char of the\n    // canonical CLDR-derived inter-field separator (e.g. `ko-KR`'s `. ` degrades\n    // to `.`). RTL locales prefix the literal with a bidi mark (e.g. `ar-EG`\n    // yields `\\u{200f}/`), so skip directionality/format marks and whitespace to\n    // land on the real delimiter. [`ars_i18n::date_field_separator`] is the\n    // shared source the segmented `date_field`/`date_time_picker` inputs use in full.\n    let separator = date_field_separator(locale)\n        .chars()\n        .find(|candidate| {\n            !candidate.is_whitespace()\n                && !candidate.is_control()\n                // Bidirectional / general format marks (LRM, RLM, ALM, etc.).\n                && !matches!(\n                    *candidate,\n                    '\\u{200e}' | '\\u{200f}' | '\\u{061c}' | '\\u{202a}'..='\\u{202e}'\n                        | '\\u{2066}'..='\\u{2069}'\n                )\n        })\n        .unwrap_or('/');"
}

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve fractional seconds in form serialization**

When a controlled or default `CalendarDateTime` contains non-zero milliseconds/microseconds/nanoseconds, this manual `HH:MM:SS` formatting silently drops the fractional part in the hidden input, so form submission no longer matches `selected_value()` even before the user edits anything. `Time` already exposes `to_iso8601()` with fractional-second preservation, so the datetime serializer should compose the date with that value instead of formatting only whole seconds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GeBxj
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:2664  reply_to=3342191929
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Localize the selected-value announcement**

For locales that use native digits or localized day-period labels, the root `aria-description` still announces ASCII digits and hard-coded `AM`/`PM` because this builds the selected datetime with `format!` instead of the component's `intl_backend`. The visible segments are localized through `format_segment_text`, so screen-reader users in those locales get an inconsistent and partially untranslated selected-value announcement.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GeBxn
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1736  reply_to=3342191935
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore roving tab stops for segments**

With more than one editable segment, this makes every segment a `Tab` stop whenever the picker is enabled, so keyboard users tab through Year/Month/Day/Hour/Minute in the browser's native order instead of the machine-managed traversal that commits buffers and moves from the last time segment to the trigger. The sibling segmented controls only expose the focused segment, or the first editable segment when none is focused, as `tabindex="0"`; this picker needs the same roving tab-stop logic to keep the documented segment navigation and focus state in sync.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GeBxq
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1215  reply_to=3342191939
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Project calendar selections before caching**

When the picker is configured for a non-Gregorian calendar but a public/custom `CalendarSelectDate` event supplies a date in another calendar, this caches the foreign display fields directly; the next publish path then reassembles those fields under `ctx.calendar`, producing a different ISO date than the one selected. The init/value paths already project dates into the active calendar, so this selection path should do the same before rebuilding segments.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

═══ PRRT_kwDORp4enM6GeBxu
file: crates/ars-components/src/date_time/date_time_picker/mod.rs:1629  reply_to=3342191943
**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not point labels at a non-labelable group**

When adapters render this part as the spec's `<label>`, the `for` target is the `Control` wrapper (`role="group"`), not a labelable form control or focusable segment, so clicking the visible label does not focus the picker and can produce invalid markup. The control is already named with `aria-labelledby`; either omit `for` here or point it at an actual focus target that adapters render.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

    pub fn to_iso8601(&self) -> String {
        format!(
            "{}-{:02}-{:02}",

    pub fn to_iso8601(&self) -> String {
        let whole_seconds = format!("{:02}:{:02}:{:02}", self.hour, self.minute, self.second);

        let fractional = u32::from(self.millisecond) * 1_000_000
            + u32::from(self.microsecond) * 1_000
            + u32::from(self.nanosecond);

        if fractional == 0 {
            return whole_seconds;
        }

        let mut fraction = format!("{fractional:09}");

        while fraction.ends_with('0') {
            fraction.pop();
        }

        format!("{whole_seconds}.{fraction}")
    }

    /// Returns the canonical ISO 8601 representation of this time.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn to_iso8601(&self) -> String {
        let whole_seconds = format!("{:02}:{:02}:{:02}", self.hour, self.minute, self.second);

        let fractional = u32::from(self.millisecond) * 1_000_000
            + u32::from(self.microsecond) * 1_000
            + u32::from(self.nanosecond);

        if fractional == 0 {
            return whole_seconds;
        }

        let mut fraction = format!("{fractional:09}");

        while fraction.ends_with('0') {
            fraction.pop();
        }

        format!("{whole_seconds}.{fraction}")
    }

    /// Adds a time duration.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns an error if the arithmetic result cannot be represented as a
    /// wall-clock time.
    pub fn add(&self, duration: TimeDuration) -> Result<Self, DateError> {
        let next = self
            .to_temporal()
            .add(&duration.to_temporal()?)
            .map_err(|error| DateError::CalendarError(error.to_string()))?;

        Ok(Self::from_temporal(next))
    }

```
fn format_announcement(ctx: &Context) -> Option<String> {
    let date = ctx.date_value.as_ref()?;
    let time = ctx.time_value.as_ref()?;

    let separator = date_field_separator(&ctx.locale);

    let (year, month, day) = (date.year(), date.month(), date.day());

    let date_str = match date_order(&ctx.locale) {
        DateOrder::MonthDayYear => format!("{month:02}{separator}{day:02}{separator}{year:04}"),
        DateOrder::DayMonthYear => format!("{day:02}{separator}{month:02}{separator}{year:04}"),
        DateOrder::YearMonthDay => format!("{year:04}{separator}{month:02}{separator}{day:02}"),
    };

    let mut time_str = format!(
        "{:02}:{:02}",
        display_hour(*time, ctx.hour_cycle),
        time.minute()
    );

    if ctx.granularity >= TimeGranularity::Second {
        time_str.push_str(&format!(":{:02}", time.second()));
    }

    if has_day_period(ctx.hour_cycle) {
        time_str.push(' ');
        time_str.push_str(if is_pm(*time) { "PM" } else { "AM" });
    }

    Some(format!("{date_str} {time_str}"))
}

  "new_string": "fn format_announcement(ctx: &Context) -> Option<String> {\n    let date = ctx.date_value.as_ref()?;\n    let time = ctx.time_value.as_ref()?;\n\n    let separator = date_field_separator(&ctx.locale);\n\n    // Localize numeric fields and the day-period label through the intl backend\n    // so the spoken announcement matches the (localized) visible segments,\n    // rather than emitting ASCII digits / hard-coded AM/PM.\n    let digits = |value: i32, width: u8| match u32::try_from(value) {\n        Ok(value) => ctx.intl_backend.format_segment_digits(\n            value,\n            NonZeroU8::new(width).expect(\"segment width is non-zero\"),\n            &ctx.locale,\n        ),\n        Err(_) => value.to_string(),\n    };\n\n    let (year, month, day) = (\n        digits(date.year(), 4),\n        digits(i32::from(date.month()), 2),\n        digits(i32::from(date.day()), 2),\n    );\n\n    let date_str = match date_order(&ctx.locale) {\n        DateOrder::MonthDayYear => format!(\"{month}{separator}{day}{separator}{year}\"),\n        DateOrder::DayMonthYear => format!(\"{day}{separator}{month}{separator}{year}\"),\n        DateOrder::YearMonthDay => format!(\"{year}{separator}{month}{separator}{day}\"),\n    };\n\n    let mut time_str = format!(\n        \"{}:{}\",\n        digits(display_hour(*time, ctx.hour_cycle), 2),\n        digits(i32::from(time.minute()), 2),\n    );\n\n    if ctx.granularity >= TimeGranularity::Second {\n        time_str.push(':');\n        time_str.push_str(&digits(i32::from(time.second()), 2));\n    }\n\n    if has_day_period(ctx.hour_cycle) {\n        time_str.push(' ');\n        time_str.push_str(&ctx.intl_backend.day_period_label(is_pm(*time), &ctx.locale));\n    }\n\n    Some(format!(\"{date_str} {time_str}\"))\n}"
}
